azure-system-config-01000.description:
The application uses environment variables/system properties.
 To migrate a Java application that uses environment variables/system properties to Azure, you can follow these recommendations:
 
 * **Identify environment variables and system properties**: Review the usage of environment variables and system properties and externalize them.

 * **Add environment variables in Azure**: You can inject any per-service configuration settings into each service as environment variables.

 * **Define system properties in JVM options**: Any system properties that the code depends on will need to be defined in JVM options.

 * Consider using**Azure App Configuration**: You can also replace the usage of environment variables with **Azure App Configuration**. By migrating to Azure App Configuration, you can centralize and manage your application's configuration settings, making it easier to maintain and update them. Azure App Configuration provides features like versioning, dynamic updates, and integration with Azure Key Vault for secure storage of sensitive configuration values.
azure-system-config-01000.title: Environment variables/system properties

jakarta-ee-version-01000.description:
Your application is not using the latest Jakarta EE version. 
Upgrading to the latest stable version ensures better performance, security, and compatibility with modern tools.
  1. Pick a Supported Version: Review the Jakarta EE release versions and choose an actively supported version.
  2. Update Your Project: Change the Jakarta EE version in your pom.xml or build.gradle.
  3. Fix Compatibility Issues: Update deprecated code, replace removed features, and ensure dependencies are compatible with the new Jakarta EE version.
  4. Thoroughly Test: Run unit, integration, and end-to-end tests to make sure everything still works after the upgrade.
jakarta-ee-version-01000.title: Jakarta EE version not latest stable

jni-native-code-00001.description:
When migrating an application that uses native processes to Azure, it's important to consider that native processes might not run in a cloud or container environment. Instead, you can refactor your application to use cloud-compatible alternatives or managed services.

 * **Identify native process dependencies**: Review all native processes used in your application and understand the purpose of each process.

 * **Evaluate and use cloud-compatible alternatives**: For each native process, look for alternative libraries, services, or APIs that provide similar functionality and are compatible with cloud environments. Replace instances of native process usage with the chosen cloud-compatible alternatives.

 * **Leverage Azure managed services**: Evaluate the use of Azure-managed services to replace certain native process functionalities.

 * **Test and validate**: Thoroughly test the updated application to ensure it works correctly with the new libraries or services. Perform functional, performance, and stress tests to validate that the application meets its requirements and can handle the expected workload.
jni-native-code-00001.title: Java Native Processes

local-storage-00001.description:
When migrating an application that relies on the file system to Azure, it's important to consider the limitations of local storage in a cloud environment.
 An application running inside a container could lose access to a file in local storage.

 The following recommendations depend on the function of the file in local storage:
 * Determine the **storage needs** for your application: Ephemeral storage or persistent storage. Ephemeral storage only persists until the cloud environment is restarted. Persistent storage is required for data that needs to persist across restarts.
 
 * If persistent storage is needed, consider **mounting Azure File Share** or **using Azure Blob Storage**. Mount Azure file share allows your application to access files via the mount location. Azure blob storage is a scalable object store for data objects, such as text or binary files.

 * **Logging**: Log to standard output and use Azure Monitor to collect and analyze the logs.

 * **Caching**: Use Azure Cache for Redis as a cache backing service.

 * **Configuration**: Store configuration in Azure App Configuration instead of using the file system. Also store configuration settings in environment variables so that they can be updated without code changes.
local-storage-00001.title: File system - Java IO

socket-communication-00000.description:
Java sockets are internal endpoints of two-way communications. They are defined by an IP address, port, and protocol (TCP/UDP).

 Socket communication is not suitable for a cloud environment because it requires fixed communication with a target host.

 Recommendation: Use Java EE standard or loosely coupled protocols such as JMS, JAX-RS, or JAX-WS for backing service interactions.
socket-communication-00000.title: Socket communication

spring-boot-to-azure-spring-boot-version.description:
The application is using the End of OSS Support of Spring Boot Version. 
With the officially supported new versions from Spring, you can get the best experience. Here are some steps you can take to update your application to the latest version of Spring Boot:

* Choose a **supported Spring Boot version**: Check out Spring Boot Support Versions, determine the most suitable supported Spring Boot version.\n\n

* **Update Spring Boot version**: Update the Spring Boot version of your application. There are automated tools like Rewrite to help you with the migration.

* **Address code compatibility**: Review your application's codebase for any potential compatibility issues with the target Spring Boot version. Update deprecated APIs or features, address any language or library changes, and ensure that your code follows best practices and standards.

* **Test thoroughly**: Execute a comprehensive testing process to verify the compatibility and functionality of your application with the new Spring Boot version. Perform unit tests, integration tests, and system tests to validate that all components and dependencies work as expected."
spring-boot-to-azure-spring-boot-version.title: Spring Boot Version is End of OSS Support

unsecure-network-protocol-00000.description:
Using secured protocols such as HTTPS and SFTP (over HTTP and FTP) should now be the norm as applications are more and more exposed and interconnected. 
This CloudReady patterns looks for unescured URI in the source code or deprecated URI libraries. 
Ideally, URLs should be replaced in your source code by secured protocols HTTPS and SFTP (and ensure the infrastructure implements these protocols for the resources your application calls, uses or references).
unsecure-network-protocol-00000.title: Use of unsecured network protocols or URI libraries

security.title: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.
security.evidence: UploadController.java:177 - Path targetFile = dir.resolve(Paths.get(fileName).getFileName()); - User-provided filename from file upload is used to construct file paths

security.title: Relative Path Traversal
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.
security.evidence: UploadController.java:177 - User input fileName from item.getName() used in path construction with Paths.get(fileName).getFileName()

security.title: Absolute Path Traversal
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize absolute path sequences such as /abs/path that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.
security.evidence: UploadController.java:157-177 - User-provided 'dir' parameter from form field and fileName both used to construct absolute paths without prior validation

security.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')
security.description: The product constructs all or part of a command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended command when it is sent to a downstream component.
security.evidence: c:\Users\zlhe\Source\Repos\airsonic-advanced\airsonic-main\src\main\java\org\airsonic\player\controller\CaptionsController.java:159 - ProcessBuilder with user-controlled command substitution: command.stream().map(i -> i.replace("%i", identifier).replace("%f", getForceFormat(format)))

security.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
security.description: The product constructs all or part of an OS command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended OS command when it is sent to a downstream component.
security.evidence: c:\Users\zlhe\Source\Repos\airsonic-advanced\airsonic-main\src\main\java\org\airsonic\player\service\metadata\FFmpegParser.java:88 - Runtime.getRuntime().exec(command.toArray(new String[0])) with externally influenced command array

security.title: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
security.description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
security.evidence: c:\Users\zlhe\Source\Repos\airsonic-advanced\airsonic-main\src\main\webapp\WEB-INF\jsp\createShare.jsp:17-18 - Unescaped output: ${model.playUrl} directly in href attribute

security.title: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')
security.description: The product constructs a string for a command to be executed by a separate component in another control sphere, but it does not properly delimit the intended arguments, options, or switches within that command string.
security.evidence: c:\Users\zlhe\Source\Repos\airsonic-advanced\airsonic-main\src\main\java\org\airsonic\player\service\TranscodingService.java:373-386 - Argument injection via transformTranscodingVariables with user-controlled substitution variables

security.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
security.description: The product constructs all or part of an SQL command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended SQL command when it is sent to a downstream component. Without sufficient removal or quoting of SQL syntax in user-controllable inputs, the generated SQL query can cause those inputs to be interpreted as SQL instead of ordinary user data.
security.evidence: c:\Users\zlhe\Source\Repos\airsonic-advanced\airsonic-main\src\main\java\org\airsonic\player\dao\AvatarDao.java:64 - SQL injection: String sql = "select " + QUERY_COLUMNS + " from system_avatar where id=" + id

security.title: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection')
security.description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before it is used as an identifier for a resource that may be outside the intended sphere of control.
security.evidence: c:\Users\zlhe\Source\Repos\airsonic-advanced\airsonic-main\src\main\java\org\airsonic\player\controller\CaptionsController.java:140-159 - Resource injection: inputFile path used in command construction with user-controlled captionId and format parameters

security.title: Use of Hard-coded Password
security.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.
security.evidence: airsonic-main/src/main/java/org/airsonic/player/security/AesGcmPasswordEncoder.java:40 - private static final String CONSTANT_PASSWORD = "airsonicencryptorpassword";

security.title: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
security.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.
security.evidence: airsonic-main/src/main/java/org/airsonic/player/service/LastFmService.java:51 - private static final String LAST_FM_KEY = "ece4499898a9440896dfdce5dab26bbf";

security.title: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
security.description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.
security.evidence: UploadController.java:169-189 - File uploads accept any file type without extension or content-type validation. No whitelist for allowed file types

security.title: Use of Obsolete Function
security.description: The code uses deprecated or obsolete functions, which suggests that the code has not been actively reviewed or maintained.
security.evidence: airsonic-main/src/main/java/org/airsonic/player/service/JukeboxService.java:64 - @Deprecated annotation on updateJukebox method

security.title: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
security.description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.
security.evidence: c:\Users\zlhe\Source\Repos\airsonic-advanced\airsonic-main\src\main\java\org\airsonic\player\service\ConfigurationPropertiesService.java:28-36 - Singleton pattern without synchronization: getInstance() checks if instance is null and calls reset() without synchronized block or volatile modifier on the instance field

security.title: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
security.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.
security.evidence: c:\Users\zlhe\Source\Repos\airsonic-advanced\airsonic-main\src\test\java\org\airsonic\player\TestCaseUtils.java:21-39 - Static non-volatile field 'airsonicHomeDirForTest' accessed and modified without synchronization in airsonicHomePathForTest() method

security.title: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
security.description: The product processes an XML document that can contain XML entities with URIs that resolve to documents outside of the intended sphere of control, causing the product to embed incorrect documents into its output.
security.evidence: SonosLinkSecurityInterceptor.java:82 - JAXBContext.newInstance().createUnmarshaller() without XXE protection; RegisterPrecompiledJSPInitializer.java:64 - Unmarshaller created without disabling external entities

security.title: Improper Synchronization
security.description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.
security.evidence: c:\Users\zlhe\Source\Repos\airsonic-advanced\airsonic-main\src\main\java\org\airsonic\player\service\ConfigurationPropertiesService.java:26-36 - Static instance field lacks proper synchronization allowing concurrent modification during getInstance() calls

security.title: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
security.description: When converting from one data type to another, such as long to integer, data can be omitted or translated in a way that produces unexpected values. If the resulting values are used in a sensitive context, then dangerous behaviors may occur.
security.evidence: airsonic-main/src/main/java/org/airsonic/player/service/jukebox/AudioPlayer.java:153 - return (int) (line.getMicrosecondPosition() / 1000000L);

security.title: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
security.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.
security.evidence: airsonic-main/src/main/java/org/airsonic/player/service/SettingsService.java:417 - Files.createDirectory(dir) without setting explicit permissions for security-critical directories

security.title: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
security.description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.
security.evidence: airsonic-main/src/main/java/org/airsonic/player/service/jukebox/PlayerTest.java:54 - new FileInputStream not closed in exception path

security.title: Missing Release of File Descriptor or Handle after Effective Lifetime
security.description: The product does not release a file descriptor or handle after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the file descriptor/handle is no longer needed.
security.evidence: airsonic-main/src/main/java/org/airsonic/player/service/jukebox/PlayerTest.java:54 - new FileInputStream not closed in exception path

security.title: Insufficient Logging
security.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.
security.evidence: airsonic-main/src/main/java/org/airsonic/player/controller/UserSettingsController.java:228-230 - Password changes executed without security event logging

security.title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
security.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
security.evidence: airsonic-main/src/main/java/org/airsonic/player/security/AesGcmPasswordEncoder.java:40 - private static final String CONSTANT_PASSWORD = "airsonicencryptorpassword";

security.title: Missing Synchronization
security.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.
security.evidence: c:\Users\zlhe\Source\Repos\airsonic-advanced\airsonic-main\src\main\java\org\airsonic\player\util\Util.java:202 - Static mutable 'validator' field accessed across threads without synchronization

security.title: Incorrect Synchronization
security.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner, but it does not correctly synchronize access to the resource.
security.evidence: c:\Users\zlhe\Source\Repos\airsonic-advanced\airsonic-main\src\main\java\org\airsonic\player\service\ConfigurationPropertiesService.java:26-36 - Incorrect synchronization: double-checked locking pattern attempted without volatile modifier on static instance field

security.title: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')
security.description: The product contains an iteration or loop with an exit condition that cannot be reached, i.e., an infinite loop.
security.evidence: airsonic-main/src/main/java/org/airsonic/player/service/jukebox/AudioPlayer.java:173 - while (true) loop; airsonic-main/src/main/java/org/airsonic/player/service/PathWatcherService.java:43 - for (;;) loop
